title: Artifact loader: shard header standardization & tokenizer adapter refactor
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Background: Over the last 18 months multiple ad-hoc weight formats and sharding metadata conventions accumulated across the model ingestion path. This has created compatibility fragility between the model registry, the runtime loader, and tokenizer adapters (different tools assume different header keys and byte-ordering for sharded checkpoints). Scope: 1) Introduce a compact, versioned shard header (rwi_shard_v2) describing shard byte ranges, dtype, compression, and quantization profile. 2) Refactor the tokenizer adapter interface so the loader and tokenizer share a single canonical byte->token offset contract (avoiding duplicated tokenization passes during load/verify). 3) Migrate the model manifest schema to include loader hints (preferred kernel layout, KV cache layout hints) to enable faster cold starts. 4) Remove legacy weight format parsers and provide a compatibility shim that translates legacy manifests to the new manifest at registry ingestion time. Goals: reduce model cold-load latency, remove fragile ad-hoc parsing code, reduce memory blow-ups from duplicated tokenizer buffers, and simplify future on-the-fly quantization work.
acceptance_criteria: New shard header spec (rwi_shard_v2) documented in the design doc and used by loader and registry
Tokenizer adapter exposes canonical byte->token offset mapping and is consumed by loader to avoid duplicate tokenization during verification
Benchmarks show >=10% median model cold-load time reduction for 7B-70B models on x86+NVIDIA (internal benchmark suite)
No increase in peak memory during model load (>2% regression threshold), and unit tests cover backward compatibility shims
CI includes a migration test that converts one sample legacy checkpoint to the new manifest and validates production inference parity
steps: Design: finalize rwi_shard_v2 header fields and compatibility rules (PRD/design doc)
Registry: implement manifest upgrade hook that emits rwi_shard_v2 and loader hints on ingest
Loader: implement parsing for rwi_shard_v2, integrate tokenizer adapter byte-offset API, and add mmap-optimized read path
Compatibility shim: add translator for legacy manifests; add tests for edge cases (partial shards, mixed dtypes)
Benchmarking: run cold-start/load-time and peak-memory benchmarks across model sizes on dedicated infra
Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag; run end-to-end smoke tests and monitor canary telemetry for regressions
decisions: Use versioned shard header 'rwi_shard_v2' (string) instead of ad-hoc keys; header placed as first bytes with small JSON body to remain extensible

Tokenizer adapter will expose a single API tokenize_with_offsets(bytes) -> token_ids + byte_offsets; loader will call this only during offline verification, not during runtime tokenization to avoid IO duplication
Keep backward compatibility via registry-time manifest translation (cheap, performed once at ingest) rather than inflating loader with many legacy parsers
Favor mmap-based loader path for Linux x86/gpu hosts and a buffered fallback for Windows/edge cases
Do not change on-disk model weight ordering in this ticket; we only add metadata/lazy read paths to avoid unsafe migrations
risks: Registry migration could be slow if a customer uploads many legacy checkpoints at once; mitigation: rate-limited background conversion and operator visibility
Tokenizer adapter API may not immediately fit language-specific tokenizers (SentencePiece variants); mitigation: adapter shim and test corpus coverage
Mmap optimization may expose subtle bugs with memory accounting and address space limits on small instances; mitigation: guardrails and telemetry thresholds
Rolling out loader changes could surface previously hidden race conditions in model caching; mitigation: thorough concurrency testing + canary rollout
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marcus Chen: Initial spike completed. Validated a compact JSON header can be embedded in the first 256 bytes of each shard; preliminary numbers show 9% improvement on 13B cold-load by avoiding a redundant tokenizer pass.
2026-03-05 - Priya Rao: Design doc uploaded and shared with Runtime and Registry teams. Requesting review from @Ava Patel (QA) and @Liam O'Connor (Infra). Added cycle estimate of 8 points.
2026-03-08 - Ava Patel: QA notes: add fuzzing for corrupted header bytes and add a test for mixed-endian shards (we have old Windows-produced checkpoints).

2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen: Implemented registry translation hook (draft). Hook registers converted manifest with 'manifest_schema: rwi_manifest_v3' and emits a migration log. Opening PR for early feedback.

2026-03-12 - Priya Rao: Loader PR added mmap path and tokenizer offset integration. Found a race in model cache eviction under heavy concurrency; added a lock around lazy-mmap initialization for now. Intend to replace with lock-free once memory accounting tests pass.

2026-03-14 - QA run: benchmark suite shows median 12% cold-load latency reduction for 7B/13B and 10% for 70B on our GPU infra; peak memory regressed by 1.5% (within threshold). Moving to canary feature-flag rollout next week.
